messages:
Elena (CFO): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands finance segment — capturing the decisions and a handful of operational Qs so teams can act.
Jon (CEO): appreciate this. please flag if any action could move runway materially.
Elena (CFO): No immediate runway change. We still model ~20-24 months on the base case. Material risks: unplanned Dedicated capacity growth and a cluster of large third-party consulting engagements slipping on approvals.
Aisha (Head of Ops): For consulting/PS, do we want a hard stop at kickoff until Finance/Legal countersign?
Elena (CFO): Yes — effective immediately: any PS/consulting > $20k requires Finance + Legal countersign before work begins. Smaller purchases follow the approval matrix.
Maya (Procurement): Posting the consolidated approval matrix and quick rules here:
```
- <= $2k: employee + manager
- $2k - $20k: manager + Finance Ops
- $20k - $100k: Director + Finance + Legal
- > $100k: VP + CFO + Legal
- Emergency (incident/remediation): on-call eng -> procurement@redwood post-facto audit
```
Sam (SWE): Slightly different from the doc we saw last month — is the $25k threshold moving down to $20k?
Luca (Finance Ops): Correct — threshold updated to $20k after review. We ran sensitivity scenarios and $20k gives better control without too much friction.
Sam (SWE): For Dedicated reservations: is there a separate flow than normal vendor spends? Eng infra owns the request but finance must sign off for large reservations, right?
Luca (Finance Ops): Flow: 1) Eng files a reservation ticket in procurement queue (include cost center tag, expected start/end, monthly $ estimate). 2) If estimated > $8k/mo, it triggers Director review; if > $20k (pro-rated), follow the $20k approval path. 3) Finance requires CC tagging for billing.
Aisha (Head of Ops): Nights/weekend incident approvals — we need a compact chain to avoid blocking incident response.
Elena (CFO): Emergency approval chain: on-call eng -> on-call SRE -> Finance Ops on-call -> CFO. Any approver can escalate to the next person; all emergency spends must have a ticket and be reviewed within 48 hours.
Sam (SWE): Can we get a one-page playbook for infra folks: how to reserve, email templates, expected fields?
Maya (Procurement): Yes. I will publish a procurement playbook in Notion by EOD tomorrow. Draft live here: https://notion.redwood/inventory/procurement-playbook (permissions pending).
devops-bot: purchase-policy.yaml updated by @Maya at 1830124950. See git link: git.redwood/policies/purchase-policy.yaml
ProcurementBot: New procurement ticket template created: `reserved-gpu-request`. Fields: requester, cost_center, start_date, end_date, est_monthly_cost, justification.
Luca (Finance Ops): A few housekeeping asks: 1) Tag all infra requests with cost center; 2) Include expected duration and cancellation policy for reservations; 3) No vendor onboarding or contractor engagement until Procurement acknowledges ticket.
Elena (CFO): Card policy changes: default corporate card limit for individual contributors lowered to $2k unless manager+finance approve an exception. Manager cards unchanged for now.
Sam (SWE): Autoscale bursts question — will autoscale that causes spend to jump >$5k/mo auto-pause?
Maya (Procurement): Not auto-pause; instead any burst that will drive incremental spend > $5k/mo triggers a flagged review and alert to Finance. If the burst is expected (known workload), Eng lead + Finance signoff OK. We will add alerting for spend deltas.
Sam (SWE): perfect. can we have the spend alerts sent to the team slack channel and finance?
Maya (Procurement): Yes, alerting to be configured to notify the owning Slack channel + finance@redwood.com.
Aisha (Head of Ops): Who owns communicating this to managers and ICs?
Elena (CFO): Aisha will coordinate rollout comms to managers; Maya publishes playbook; Luca publishes tagging examples and a short FAQ with request examples.
Luca (Finance Ops): I will post the FAQ tomorrow AM with two examples: 1) Reserved GPU request 2) PS contract procurement flow.
Jon (CEO): thanks team — once live, @channel the docs and link the playbook in the all-hands notes. Keeping runway visibility high is critical.
Sam (SWE): reviewed and will bookmark the playbook.
Elena (CFO): Closing thread — if there are edge cases or urgent blockers, DM me. Thanks for the quick alignment! :rocket:
